definition: Enthusiastic public praise or approval.
sentence: The school acclaimed Marcus as a culinary genius after he discovered that frozen waffles taste better when you actually cook them.

definition: Sharp, severe, or intense; also highly perceptive.
sentence: I developed acute embarrassment when my phone connected to the restaurant speakers and began playing whale sounds at full volume.

definition: To state or confirm that something is true.
sentence: Grandma solemnly affirmed that she had eaten only one cookie, while three more were visibly protruding from her purse.

definition: To make a problem, condition, or situation worse.
sentence: Trying to fix the leaking sink with a hammer only aggravated the problem and introduced the kitchen to indoor rain.

definition: Foreign, unfamiliar, or belonging to another place or group.
sentence: The concept of waking up voluntarily before 7:00 a.m. was completely alien to Trevor.

definition: A person, group, or nation joined with another for mutual support.
sentence: I gained a powerful ally in the battle for the last doughnut when Grandma quietly slid the box toward me.

definition: A remedy that counteracts a poison or harmful effect.
sentence: The only known antidote to Uncle Larry's three-hour slideshow was pretending the house was on fire.

definition: Old-fashioned and no longer useful or appropriate.
sentence: Dad's antiquated GPS instructed us to turn onto a road that has apparently been a lake since 1994.

definition: Widely told or believed but of doubtful or unknown authenticity.
sentence: The apocryphal family story claims Grandpa once wrestled an alligator, although Grandpa describes the animal as 'possibly a large handbag.'

definition: Anxiety or fear about something that may happen.
sentence: I approached the dentist with apprehension after hearing a drill and someone yell, 'Well, that's new.'

definition: Based on random choice or personal whim rather than a clear reason or rule.
sentence: The referee's arbitrary rule declared that goals scored while wearing purple socks counted double on Tuesdays.

definition: Not representative of the usual type or pattern.
sentence: It was atypical of our cat to greet visitors warmly, so we immediately checked whether he had been replaced by an impostor.

definition: Commanding trust or respect because of knowledge, confidence, or official status.
sentence: The eight-year-old gave an authoritative lecture on dinosaurs despite repeatedly pronouncing 'Jurassic' as 'Jurassical.'

definition: Extreme greed for wealth or material gain.
sentence: His avarice became obvious when he charged his own grandmother a convenience fee for passing the salt.

definition: To state or admit something openly and firmly.
sentence: I avowed my innocence in the missing-cake investigation despite having frosting on both eyebrows.

definition: Harmless, gentle, or not dangerous.
sentence: The creature under my bed turned out to be benign: it was merely a sock wearing another sock.

definition: Something that damages, spoils, or destroys; to cause such damage.
sentence: The giant inflatable flamingo was a blight on the elegant garden, according to everyone except the flamingo's extremely proud owner.

definition: Something highly beneficial or helpful.
sentence: Noise-canceling headphones were a boon during my brother's brief but passionate career as a recorder soloist.

definition: Unlimited or seemingly without end.
sentence: Grandma displayed boundless patience while Grandpa attempted to reset the Wi-Fi by repeatedly unplugging the toaster.

definition: Large, strong, and heavily built.
sentence: The burly security guard looked terrifying until a butterfly landed on him and he whispered, 'Hello, tiny friend.'

definition: Bitingly sarcastic or harsh; chemically able to burn or corrode.
sentence: Her caustic review of my singing suggested that silence had been one of humanity's greatest inventions.

definition: To criticize or punish someone severely.
sentence: Mom chastised us for launching grapes across the dining room as though we had violated international law.

definition: To scold or gently criticize.
sentence: Grandma chided me for eating dessert before dinner, then quietly handed me a second brownie.

definition: The use of more words than necessary, especially to avoid saying something directly.
sentence: Through heroic circumlocution, Dad took eleven minutes to say that he had forgotten to buy milk.

definition: To force or strongly drive someone to do something.
sentence: The smell of fresh pizza compelled me to enter the kitchen despite having sworn eternal loyalty to my diet nine minutes earlier.

definition: Too self-satisfied to notice or address possible problems.
sentence: I became complacent after winning three chess games against my little cousin, who then revealed she had been moving the pieces randomly.

definition: An agreement reached by mutual concessions; also to weaken or endanger something.
sentence: We compromised: my brother got the window seat, and I got the right to complain about it for the entire flight.

definition: Excessive pride in oneself; also an elaborate idea or literary device.
sentence: His conceit was extraordinary: after microwaving soup successfully, he began referring to himself as 'Chef Antonio.'

definition: Expressing much in few words; brief and clear.
sentence: Asked to give a concise review of the hotel, Dad said, 'Bed good. Shower weird. Goose hostile.'

definition: To agree or share the same opinion.
sentence: I concurred with the dog that the vacuum cleaner was suspicious and should not be trusted.

definition: Thoughtful about other people's needs and feelings.
sentence: It was considerate of Leo to warn us before practicing the trumpet, although six seconds was not much evacuation time.

definition: Opposite in nature, direction, or meaning; stubbornly opposed.
sentence: Contrary to Dad's prediction, assembling the trampoline did require the instructions, three neighbors, and a brief period of prayer.

definition: Friendly, cheerful, and enjoyable, especially in company.
sentence: The dinner was convivial until Uncle Pete introduced a spreadsheet ranking everyone's potato-salad contributions.

definition: Familiar with and influenced by many cultures; sophisticated and worldly.
sentence: After eating sushi twice, Kevin became cosmopolitan enough to criticize the airport food in three languages he did not speak.

definition: Believable or worthy of trust.
sentence: My story about the broken lamp became less credible when I blamed 'a highly organized squirrel syndicate.'

definition: Boldly resisting authority, rules, or opposition.
sentence: The defiant toddler stared directly at his father while lowering one pea at a time onto the floor.

definition: The death, end, or failure of something.
sentence: The demise of my houseplant occurred after I watered it lovingly with what turned out to be iced coffee.

definition: To move someone to a lower rank, position, or status.
sentence: After the dog ate the payroll, he was demoted from office mascot to unpaid hallway consultant.

definition: To represent or show in words, art, or another medium.
sentence: The mural depicted George Washington crossing the Delaware, except someone had added sunglasses and a jet ski.

definition: Empty, abandoned, bleak, or deeply lonely.
sentence: The refrigerator looked desolate after my cousins visited: one pickle, half a lemon, and a mustard bottle staring into the void.

definition: A loud, unpleasant, prolonged noise.
sentence: The din from the children's birthday party made the leaf blower outside sound like a meditation app.

definition: To perceive, recognize, or distinguish something clearly.
sentence: Through the fog, I could barely discern the shape ahead until it mooed and clarified the situation.

definition: Impartial and not influenced by personal advantage.
sentence: We needed a disinterested judge for the cookie contest, so naturally we did not choose the Labrador.

definition: Clearly different or separate; unmistakable.
sentence: There was a distinct smell of burnt toast, followed by the distinct sound of Dad denying responsibility.

definition: To reveal information that was private or secret.
sentence: Under intense questioning, my sister divulged the location of the hidden candy stash and immediately entered witness protection.

definition: Striking, sudden, or exaggerated in effect or behavior.
sentence: Grandma made a dramatic entrance to breakfast by announcing, 'I have survived the upstairs staircase once again!'

definition: Made up of elements drawn from many different sources or styles.
sentence: His eclectic playlist jumped from Mozart to heavy metal to whale songs, often within the same minute.

definition: A basic or essential part of something.
sentence: An essential element of Dad's famous chili is secrecy, mostly because nobody wants to know what is actually in it.

definition: To steal money or property entrusted to one's care.
sentence: The treasurer was accused of embezzling bake-sale funds after arriving at school in a suspiciously frosting-colored sports car.

definition: To pronounce words clearly and distinctly.
sentence: The drama teacher told me to enunciate, so I announced 'PASS THE KETCHUP' as though addressing Parliament.

definition: To destroy or remove completely.
sentence: Dad vowed to eradicate the ants, but the ants appeared to have lawyers, zoning approval, and a long-term lease.

definition: To adopt, support, or advocate a belief or cause.
sentence: My cousin espouses minimalist living while owning fourteen decorative pillows labeled 'essential.'

definition: To make a problem, feeling, or situation worse.
sentence: Telling Mom to 'calm down' only exacerbated the situation, a finding now supported by extensive family research.

definition: Worthy of imitation because it is exceptionally good.
sentence: Her exemplary behavior at dinner lasted until dessert, when she attempted to drink pudding through a straw.

definition: Extremely thorough and covering all possibilities or details.
sentence: Dad conducted an exhaustive search for his glasses while wearing them on his face.

definition: Convenient and effective for a particular purpose, though possibly improper or imperfect.
sentence: Using duct tape as a belt was expedient, although it complicated the evening considerably.

definition: To make effective use of something; or to use someone unfairly for one's own benefit.
sentence: My brother exploited my fear of spiders by charging me two dollars to remove what turned out to be a raisin.
synonyms: use; capitalize on; manipulate; take advantage of

definition: To invent something false; also to construct or manufacture.
sentence: I fabricated an elaborate excuse involving a meteor, but the teacher unfortunately had access to weather reports.

definition: Based on mistaken reasoning or a false idea.
sentence: His fallacious argument was that vegetables are unhealthy because nobody has ever seen a rabbit driving a car.

definition: To abandon or give up someone or something.
sentence: I swore never to forsake my diet, then encountered a cheesecake and respectfully revised my position.

definition: Direct, honest, and straightforward.
sentence: The forthright waiter said, 'Do not order the fish,' then stared meaningfully toward the kitchen.

definition: To distort, confuse, or reproduce a message inaccurately.
sentence: The broken speaker garbled the principal's announcement into what sounded like, 'All students may now release the goats.'

definition: A person who eats or consumes excessively.
sentence: At the buffet, my glutton of a cousin built a mashed-potato mountain visible from neighboring counties.

definition: Kind, courteous, and pleasantly generous.
sentence: Our gracious host smiled warmly even after I knocked over the centerpiece and baptized the tablecloth in gravy.

definition: To irritate or annoy; also to shred into small pieces.
sentence: His habit of humming one note continuously began to grate on everyone except the cheese, which had other concerns.

definition: Unnecessary, uncalled for, or given without charge.
sentence: The movie contained a gratuitous twelve-minute chase scene involving tractors, penguins, and absolutely no relevance to the plot.

definition: To shelter or conceal; also to hold a thought or feeling over time.
sentence: I harbored resentment toward the vending machine after it accepted my dollar and returned nothing but a judgmental hum.

definition: Forming a pleasing or consistent whole; free from conflict.
sentence: The family reunion remained harmonious until someone asked who made the superior potato salad.

definition: Deliberate exaggeration used for emphasis or effect.
sentence: Saying I waited 'a thousand years' for the microwave was hyperbole, although those final six seconds were brutal.

definition: Distinctive or peculiar to a particular person or thing.
sentence: Grandpa's idiosyncratic filing system stores tax documents alphabetically by the first food he ate that day.

definition: Based on an illusion; not real despite seeming real.
sentence: My sense of financial security was illusory because I had forgotten about the automatic renewal for Premium Goat Facts.

definition: Unable to be calmed, satisfied, or persuaded to change.
sentence: The implacable toddler rejected crackers, toys, songs, negotiations, and finally the concept of civilization itself.

definition: To put a plan, decision, or system into effect.
sentence: We implemented a new household rule requiring everyone to label leftovers, which Dad immediately labeled 'Probably Fine.'

definition: Made poor or lacking in resources, quality, or richness.
sentence: After buying three concert tickets, I was financially impoverished but spiritually rich in terrible seats.

definition: Too minor or unimportant to have much effect.
sentence: The typo was inconsequential until the birthday banner read 'Happy 80th, Brian' for a six-year-old.

definition: A recess, notch, or inward space; also the spacing at the start of a line of text.
sentence: The mysterious indentation in the couch turned out to be Grandpa, who had been napping there since lunch.

definition: Habitually lazy or avoiding effort.
sentence: The indolent cat watched a mouse walk past and appeared to decide that predation was not in his job description.

definition: Overly willing to satisfy someone's wishes or excuse their behavior.
sentence: The indulgent grandfather responded to 'Can I have one cookie?' by purchasing the bakery.

definition: Incapable of making mistakes or being wrong.
sentence: Dad claimed his sense of direction was infallible moments before we arrived at the same gas station for the third time.

definition: Impossible or extremely difficult to overcome.
sentence: The locked cookie jar presented an insuperable obstacle until Grandma revealed that the lid simply twisted off.

definition: Able to be understood.
sentence: The toddler's speech became intelligible only after she pointed furiously at the cookie jar.

definition: Thoughtfully examining one's own thoughts, feelings, or motives.
sentence: After eating the last brownie, Kevin became introspective and asked himself whether he was selfish; then he licked the plate.

definition: So good or proper that no criticism is deserved.
sentence: Her table manners were irreproachable until a pea rolled away and she pursued it with a fork like a tiny spearman.

definition: Using very few words.
sentence: Asked how his first skydiving trip went, Ben gave the laconic reply, 'Parachute worked.'

definition: Broad-minded or open to change; also generous in amount or application.
sentence: The chef was liberal with the garlic, to the point that vampires began avoiding the entire zip code.

definition: Amusement, laughter, or cheerful happiness.
sentence: The sight of Dad trapped inside the inflatable snowman produced considerable mirth and several unhelpful photographs.

definition: To change something, usually partially rather than completely.
sentence: I modified the recipe by replacing two tablespoons of sugar with an entire bag of marshmallows and calling it research.

definition: Indirect, slanting, or not expressed straightforwardly.
sentence: Mom made an oblique reference to my messy room by asking whether raccoons had recently moved upstairs.

definition: No longer in use because something newer has replaced it.
sentence: My flip phone became obsolete sometime between 'Snake II' and everyone else acquiring the internet.

definition: Causing anger or disgust; also relating to attacking rather than defending.
sentence: His joke was offensive enough that even the parrot stopped repeating it.

definition: Highly decorated with elaborate details.
sentence: The ornate cake had gold leaves, sugar roses, tiny columns, and almost nowhere left to put actual cake.

definition: Not active or assertive; accepting what happens without resistance.
sentence: The passive dog watched the squirrel steal his biscuit and seemed to regard the incident as an administrative matter.

definition: The outer edge or boundary of an area or subject.
sentence: I stood at the periphery of the dance floor, where people with my rhythm are legally safest.

definition: Self-important and excessively grand in speech or manner.
sentence: The pompous waiter described tap water as 'a locally sourced transparent beverage with mineral undertones.'

definition: Having great power, influence, or effect.
sentence: The garlic sauce was so potent that opening the container caused three people to remember appointments elsewhere.

definition: To talk at length in a foolish or trivial way.
sentence: Uncle Dan prattled about his new lawn mower until even the lawn looked bored.

definition: Happening too early or before the proper time.
sentence: My victory dance was premature because the bowling ball had not yet reached the pins and was, in fact, headed toward another lane.

definition: Trying to appear more important, cultured, or sophisticated than one really is.
sentence: The pretentious café served toast on a wooden plank and called crumbs 'artisanal fragments.'

definition: Showing disrespect toward sacred things; also vulgar or irreverent.
sentence: The monk considered my ringtone during the ceremony profane, particularly because it was a duck quacking the national anthem.

definition: Very deep, intense, or intellectually significant.
sentence: After staring into the refrigerator for ten minutes, I reached the profound conclusion that we needed groceries.

definition: An introductory section of a literary or dramatic work.
sentence: The play's prologue explained the ancient family feud, the cursed necklace, and why everyone was inexplicably dressed as a lobster.

definition: To make something last longer.
sentence: Asking Grandpa one question about trains prolonged dinner by approximately forty-seven historical anecdotes.

definition: Correct or socially acceptable behavior.
sentence: A debate arose over the propriety of wearing swim goggles to a funeral; Uncle Fred claimed they were 'formal black.'

definition: Ordinary, dull, or lacking imagination.
sentence: The magician's grand finale was painfully prosaic: he checked his email and folded laundry.

definition: To make something continue longer than necessary or expected.
sentence: Dad protracted the goodbye by remembering six additional stories while already standing in the driveway.

definition: Showing careful judgment and concern for future consequences.
sentence: It was prudent to read the label before drinking the bottle marked 'Industrial Strength Jalapeño Concentrate.'

definition: A long, angry, impassioned complaint or speech.
sentence: Dad's rant about printer ink began at breakfast and achieved a surprising second act during dessert.

definition: Based on reason or logical thought.
sentence: A rational person would have called pest control; Trevor named the raccoon Gerald and gave him a key.

definition: A treatment or action that corrects a problem.
sentence: Grandma's remedy for nearly every illness involved tea, sleep, and an amount of soup requiring municipal permits.

definition: An expression of criticism or disapproval.
sentence: The teacher's raised eyebrow was a more effective reproof than the entire lecture that followed.

definition: To set aside for future use; also restraint in expressing emotion.
sentence: I reserved the last piece of cake by writing my name on it, surrounding it with tape, and hiring the dog as security.

definition: Very bright, attractive, or impressive in appearance.
sentence: Grandpa appeared resplendent in a purple tuxedo, silver shoes, and the confidence of a man unaware of subtlety.

definition: Basic, undeveloped, or involving only the simplest principles.
sentence: My rudimentary knowledge of plumbing consisted of knowing that water should generally remain inside the pipes.

definition: A break, burst, or tear; to break or burst.
sentence: The water balloon ruptured directly above Dad, abruptly ending his lecture on responsible summer behavior.

definition: Showing no pity or compassion in pursuing a goal.
sentence: Grandma was ruthless at Scrabble and once challenged a seven-year-old's spelling of 'cat.'

definition: To officially authorize something; also to impose a penalty for violating rules.
sentence: The school sanctioned the pie-eating contest but imposed sanctions when Trevor attempted to use a leaf blower.

definition: To sparkle or flash; figuratively, to be brilliantly lively or clever.
sentence: Her conversation scintillated until someone mentioned tax forms, at which point the entire table became spiritually absent.

definition: To become or make less tight, intense, active, or severe.
sentence: Dad refused to slacken his grip on the roof rack until we explained that the car had been parked for twenty minutes.

definition: Dark, serious, or gloomy in mood.
sentence: The mood became somber when the waiter announced that the restaurant had run out of french fries.

definition: Occurring irregularly or only occasionally.
sentence: My exercise routine was sporadic: vigorous on January 2, absent until April, and briefly revived after seeing a staircase.

definition: Not moving or changing; remaining in one state.
sentence: The line remained static for so long that two customers exchanged holiday cards and one started a family.

definition: Enduring pain or difficulty without showing much emotion.
sentence: He remained stoic after stepping on a Lego, although a single tear rolled down his cheek with tremendous dignity.

definition: The act of yielding to authority; also something formally presented for consideration.
sentence: My essay submission was two days late and included a note requesting mercy from 'the academic authorities.'

definition: Willing to obey or yield to another's authority.
sentence: The supposedly submissive dog obeyed every command except 'come,' 'stay,' 'sit,' and anything involving personal inconvenience.

definition: Lower in rank, importance, or position; to place in a lower position.
sentence: As assistant assistant snack manager, I was subordinate to nearly everyone except the napkin intern.

definition: Luxuriously rich, splendid, or expensive.
sentence: The hotel served a sumptuous breakfast featuring twelve pastries, smoked salmon, and a butter sculpture with better posture than mine.

definition: An amount greater than what is needed.
sentence: We had a surplus of zucchini so enormous that neighbors began locking their cars to prevent anonymous vegetable donations.

definition: Balanced correspondence of parts on opposite sides or around a center.
sentence: The cake had perfect symmetry until Uncle Bob removed a fist-sized piece from the left side 'for testing.'

definition: Moderate and restrained; also having a mild climate.
sentence: Her temperate response to the spilled paint was impressive: she merely closed her eyes and whispered the alphabet twice.

definition: Uncertain, hesitant, or not yet final.
sentence: I gave the suspicious casserole a tentative poke with my fork, and it seemed to poke back.

definition: To move unsteadily as if about to fall.
sentence: Grandpa tottered across the icy driveway carrying six grocery bags and refusing all assistance on philosophical grounds.

definition: Complete agreement among everyone involved.
sentence: The family achieved rare unanimity on one issue: nobody wanted Uncle Carl to sing another verse.

definition: Fundamental or existing beneath the surface.
sentence: The underlying cause of the argument was not politics, money, or philosophy; it was who had eaten the last mozzarella stick.

definition: To seize a position, power, or right without authority.
sentence: My younger brother usurped my position as TV-remote holder by sitting on it and denying its existence.

definition: Able to adapt to many different functions, activities, or situations.
sentence: The versatile spatula flipped pancakes, opened a stubborn drawer, and briefly served as a microphone during breakfast karaoke.

definition: Absolutely necessary or essential; full of life and energy.
sentence: Coffee was vital to the morning meeting, especially after someone scheduled it for 7:15 a.m. without consulting civilization.

definition: Very large in volume, quantity, or extent.
sentence: The lawyer's voluminous report contained 600 pages, three appendices, and apparently the complete history of paper.

definition: Cautious and alert because of possible danger or problems.
sentence: I grew wary when the toddler said, 'Don't worry, I fixed it,' while holding a screwdriver and standing beside the television.
